title: Adaptive prefetch + health-aware routing cookbook
content:
Purpose

Quick operational cookbook for a combined adaptive-prefetch + health-aware routing policy. Goal: reduce p95 latency for user-facing requests while keeping per-token cost within the budget and avoiding reliability regressions during regional incidents. This is intentionally pragmatic: heuristics, guardrails, and a decision-tree that the control plane can execute.

Context / motivation

- We have three deployment modes (hosted, dedicated, private) and multi-region capacity.
- Pure cost-first routing (cheapest model/region) increases latency/regret for tail users.
- Pure latency-first routing wastes expensive capacity and can exhaust hot regions during spikes.
- Health incidents (degraded GPUs, congestion, infra restarts) require graceful fallbacks before user-visible errors rise.

High-level idea

1) Maintain a fast in-memory HealthScore for every (region, model-variant, capacity-pool) computed from recent latency percentiles, error rate, and queue depth.
2) Maintain a PrefetchConfidence for frequent prefixes or session contexts derived from cached KV hits and prior-request completion probability. Prefetch triggers optional warm-up calls to KV/cache or speculative token-generation on cheaper lanes.
3) The control plane evaluates a three-stage decision tree for each request: Eligibility -> Preferential Scoring -> Final Selection + Fallback Policy.

Metrics we use (signals)

- latency_p50/p95/p99 (per region/model routing-label)
- infra_error_rate (5m)
- queue_utilization (instant + 1m avg)
- token_cost_estimate (per-model per-token effective cost)
- recent_kv_hit_rate (per-prefix, windowed)
- regional_slo_breach_count (24h)
- rollout_canary_flags (on/off)

Decision tree (operational steps, trimmed for runtime efficiency)

Step A: Eligibility checks (fast rejects)
- If model variant is incompatible with request features (e.g., tool-calling, long-kv) -> ineligible.
- If tenant is on Dedicated/Private with hard pin -> route to pinned pool.
- If HealthScore(region, model) < MIN_HEALTH_THRESHOLD -> mark as deprioritized (skip unless no alternatives).

Step B: Preferential scoring (score candidates by weighted utility)
Score = w_latency * normalized_latency + w_reliability * normalized_reliability + w_cost * normalized_cost + w_prefetch * prefetch_boost
- normalized_latency: map p95 to [0,1] (lower is better)
- normalized_reliability: inverse of infra_error_rate and SLA_breach_count
- normalized_cost: linear scaled cost per token (lower cost higher score)
- prefetch_boost: +0.05..+0.25 based on PrefetchConfidence for this prefix/session

Weight guidelines (example initial values to tune)
- w_latency = 0.50
- w_reliability = 0.30
- w_cost = 0.15
- w_prefetch = 0.05
Notes: these are runtime-configurable and decomposed per-customer profile (enterprise vs free tier).

Step C: Final selection with blast radius controls
- Sort top-K candidates by Score. K default 3.
- If top candidate is > margin_threshold (default 0.08) above next -> choose it.
- Else run short probabilistic canary selection among top-K to keep utilization balanced.

Fallback policy (multi-tier)
- Soft fallback: reroute to model-variant with slightly higher latency but better reliability. Used when infra_error_rate > ERROR_RATE_SOFT or HealthScore drops gradually.
- Hard fallback: when queue_utilization > 90% or instance restarts detected -> immediate fallback to preconfigured fallback pool (possibly smaller model) and emit mitigation event.
- Degraded outputs: if model returns malformed or hallucinated output above threshold, reroute subsequent requests for session to conservative-model for N requests.

Health scoring details (sketch)
HealthScore = alpha * (1 - clamped_error_rate) + beta * (1 - normalized_p95_over_target) + gamma * (1 - normalized_queue_util)
- clamped_error_rate = min(0.2, infra_error_rate_recent)
- normalized_p95_over_target = (observed_p95 - target_p95)/(target_p95 * 3) clipped [0,1]
- normalized_queue_util = queue_util / max_queue
- weights [alpha,beta,gamma] default [0.45,0.35,0.20]
Rationale: keep error rate as highest severity signal.

Prefetch patterns and warm-up
- Track high-frequency prefixes by LRU with exponential decay; maintain per-prefix PrefetchConfidence = (#complete_first_token_hits)/(#attempts + smoothing)
- When PrefetchConfidence > 0.7 AND predicted latency benefit > threshold -> trigger warm-up: a zero-cost speculative request to reserve cache/KV or primed KV cache call.
- Warm-up should be rate-limited per tenant and globally to avoid creating load. Use per-tenant budget tokens that refill slowly.

Control plane integration
- Policy DSL (very small example):
  route_rule {
    id: "latency_cost_balance_v2"
    priority: 100
    match: { tenant_tier: "standard", region_pref: ["us-west-2","us-east-1"] }
    weights: { latency: 0.5, reliability: 0.3, cost: 0.15, prefetch: 0.05 }
    min_health: 0.55
    fallback: ["conservative-1","conservative-2"]
    prefetch: { enabled: true, budget_per_min: 10 }
  }
- Control plane exposes endpoints: evaluate_candidates(request_context) -> candidate_list_with_scores, subscribe_to_health_updates(region/model)
- All policy changes must be auditable: store policy version, who applied, and percent rollout.

Multi-region considerations and cross-region tradeoffs
- Latency tail favors routing to nearby regions but cost/reliability may favor cross-region fallbacks. Add a region_penalty to normalized_latency that encodes egress cost + regulatory constraints.
- For privacy-sensitive tenants, region preference is an eligibility constraint, not a soft penalty.
- Use sticky-session heuristics: if session has affinity to a region and HealthScore stable, prefer same region to keep KV/cache warm.

Operational playbooks (incident snippets)
- Symptom: sudden p95 jump in us-east-1 and infra_error_rate rising
  1) Control plane sets min_health for us-east-1 to 0.7 -> deprioritize for new requests.
  2) Auto-fallback moves 40% of new traffic to us-west-2 for 5 minutes then evaluate.
  3) If retries/errors persist, move to hard fallback and open on-call incident.

- Symptom: a spike in prefetch warm-up causing unexpected load
  1) Throttle prefetch globally by lowering budget_per_min for route rules to 1.
  2) Identify top prefixes causing warm-ups and add temporary blocklist.

Testing, rollout, and observability
- Canary rules: enable policy for X% of traffic or for specific user segments; monitor delta p95 and cost per token.
- Key dashboards: top-K candidate score distributions, HealthScore heatmap, prefetch hit rates, warm-up error rate, fallback counts, per-tenant cost delta.
- Retro criteria: if canary increases p95 by > 5% or cost per token by > 15% for 30m -> rollback.

Open questions / TODOs
- What exact decay window for PrefetchConfidence balances recency vs stability? (1h vs 24h experiment)
- How to normalize costs across heterogeneous hardware (A100 vs H100 vs CPU)? Need a per-architecture cost model, factoring batch efficiency.
- Decide safe default weights per tenant tier; e.g., free-tier might be cost-focused, enterprise latency-focused.
- Need a simulation harness to run synthetic traffic and measure policy regret under hybrid incidents. (JIRA-ENG-4921)

Action items
- [ ] Implement HealthScore basic aggregator (Marcus) — PR draft exists: linked_artifacts.
- [ ] Add per-prefix prefetch LRU store and budgeter (Priya).
- [ ] Build lightweight policy evaluator that runs at edge and consults control plane for policy versions (Liam).
- [ ] Create simulation scenarios and run A/B with traffic from staging (Sofia).

Notes to self
- Keep runtime evaluation under ~500us for simple requests (avoid heavy ML-based ranking in hot path).
- Be conservative with prefetch: user-visible latency wins but not at cost of saturating capacity.

References and inspiration
- Past routing playbooks in this folder (see related docs)
- Internal convo: Slack thread linked in linked_artifacts

Rough sketch of decision-tree (compact, copyable)
1) If tenant pinned -> route pinned
2) Else if HealthScore(candidate) < min_health -> deprioritize candidate
3) Build top-K candidate list
4) Compute Score for each
5) If score_gap(top1, top2) > margin -> pick top1 else probabilistic choose
6) If queue_utilization(candidate) > 90% -> immediate fallback
7) If PrefetchConfidence(prefix) > 0.7 and budget available -> attempt warm-up for chosen candidate

End of notes.

If you disagree with any heuristics or want to prototype an alternative scoring function, add to comments and tag owners.
